# Jubilees Chapter 8 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Division of the Earth; Canaan Seizes Shem's Territory

---

**8:1** In the twenty-ninth jubilee, in the first week, in the first year of it, Arpachshad took a wife named Rasu'eja, daughter of Susan daughter of Elam, and she bore him a son in the third year of that week.

**8:2** He named him Kainam. The son grew and his father taught him writing, and he went out to find a place where he might take possession of a city for himself.

**8:3** He found an inscription which earlier generations had carved on a rock. He read what was written there and transcribed it, and sinned because of it — for it contained the teaching of the Watchers by which they used to observe the omens of the sun, moon, and stars in all the signs of heaven.

**8:4** He copied it down and said nothing about it, because he was afraid to tell Noah, fearing that Noah would be angry with him.

**8:5** In the thirtieth jubilee, in the second week, in the first year of it, he took a wife named Melka, daughter of Madai son of Japheth, and in the fourth year he fathered a son and named him Shelah.

**8:6** In the thirty-first jubilee, in the first week, in the second year of it, Shelah took a wife named Mu'ak, daughter of Kesed his father's brother.

**8:7** She bore him a son in the fifth year, and he named him Eber. Then Eber took a wife named 'Azurad, daughter of Nebrod, in the thirty-second jubilee, in the seventh week, in the third year.

**8:8** In the first year of the thirty-third jubilee she bore him a son, and he named him Peleg — for in the days of his birth the children of Noah began to divide the earth among themselves; that is why he named him Peleg.

**8:9** They divided it secretly among themselves and reported it to Noah.

**8:10** It came to pass at the beginning of the thirty-third jubilee that they divided the earth into three portions for Shem, Ham, and Japheth, according to the inheritance of each, in the first year of the first week, when one of us was sent to instruct them.

**8:11** Noah called his sons; they came near — they and their children — and he divided the earth by lot among his three sons. They reached forward and drew their portions from the bosom of Noah their father.

**8:12** The lot that came forth as Shem's was the middle of the earth — to be his inheritance for himself and his sons for all generations — from the middle of the mountain range of Rafa, from the mouth of the waters of the river Tina. His portion extends westward through the midst of this river until it reaches the waters of the abyss from which this river flows out and pours into the sea Maat, and this river flows into the great sea.

**8:13** Everything to the north is Japheth's, and everything to the south belongs to Shem.

**8:14** It extends to the west of Asshur, and from there extends westward to the western sea, continuing west to reach the sea of Ailt.

**8:15** From Atel it goes eastward to the sea of Girit, and from there eastward again to the Red Sea, and from there northward to the sea of Girit and north again to the river Tina.

**8:16** This is the sea called the Red Sea — stretching from Atel and from the great sea to the sea called Maat, and extending to the sea called Girit.

**8:17** It extends westward from the sea of Girit along the sea of Tirrin toward the sea of Girit, and from the sea of Tirrin eastward to the sea of Asshur.

**8:18** From there it goes to Mount Rafa on the north side of that mountain — this is the northern limit of Shem's portion.

**8:19** This is the land assigned to Shem and his sons as their inheritance, which they shall possess for all generations: five great islands and a great land in the east.

**8:20** The second portion that came forth was for Ham: beyond the Gihon to the south, to the right of the Garden. It extends southward to all the mountains of fire, and westward to the sea of Atel, and westward until it reaches the sea called the sea of Mauk — that sea from which nothing that descends into it from the face of all the earth ever rises again — until the day of the great judgment when all who have corrupted their ways and their works before God are judged.

**8:21** It extends northward to the limits of Gadir and to the coastal waters of the sea.

**8:22** The third portion came forth for Japheth: beyond the river Tina to the north of its outflow, extending north-eastward to the entire region of Gog and all the east thereof.

**8:23** It extends northward to the north, to the mountains of Qelt in the north and to the sea of Mauk, and eastward of Gadir as far as the region of the waters of the sea.

**8:24** This is the land assigned to Japheth and his sons as their inheritance, which they shall possess for all generations: five great islands and a great land in the north.

**8:25** The land of Japheth is cold, the land of Ham is hot, and the land of Shem is neither hot nor cold but a blend of the two.

**8:26** The land of Ham extends from the sea of Mauk to the sea of Atel.

**8:27** Then Canaan saw the land of Lebanon as far as the Jordan and the coast of the sea, and he seized it for himself. Neither his father Ham nor his brothers Mizraim, Put, and Cush took it away from him.

**8:28** He settled in the land of Lebanon from Hamath to the entrance of Egypt — he and his sons — and they have lived there to this day.

**8:29** Therefore the land of Canaan is accursed, destined to be a servant — because he settled in the lot of Shem, and all the sons of Shem are to drive him out as an accursed one, for it is not his portion according to Ham's lot. Those who dwelt in the land of Canaan acted wickedly.

**8:30** Ham knew that his father had cursed his younger son Canaan, and he was displeased that Canaan had seized the inheritance of Shem.

---
*SOPHIA notes: Consensus follows LOGOS throughout. The sea of Mauk description (v.20) — "that sea from which nothing... ever rises again" — preserved verbatim as a significant Jubilees cosmic geography motif. The Canaan land-seizure (vv.27-30) preserved in full as the chapter's theological climax.*
